sources.title: Remo Kretschmann and Frank Werner, Maximum a posteriori testing in statistical inverse problems
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 34-page PDF and read the complete passages for the indexed white-noise model, the adjoint-range restriction for unregularized features, Gaussian posterior feature law and MAP probe, weighted Tikhonov representation under covariance/normal-operator commutation, exact raw MAP size and power, the non-eigenfeature level-one theorem and its proof, and the same-sample prior-tuning caveat. The paper's compact-model setting is retained where invoked; the local weighted identity is proved directly under the stated trace-class prior assumptions.

contents.name: Unregularized one-probe feature restriction and indexed Gaussian observation model
contents.support: Supports the one-probe linear observation convention and the source restriction to adjoint-range features; the local definition proves the exact unbiasedness/range equivalence directly.

contents.name: Gaussian posterior feature marginal and MAP probe
contents.support: Supports the Gaussian conditioning formula and posterior feature mean/covariance; the local proof constructs the posterior kernel on the cylinder observation sigma-algebra.

contents.name: Posterior-marginal MAP feature test
contents.support: Supports the half-space test obtained by comparing the scalar posterior Gaussian mode with zero. The local raw rule is defined for every field input; its posterior-mode interpretation holds only P_Y-almost surely for each fixed feature, matching the actual posterior-law supplier.

contents.name: Weighted Tikhonov characterization and exact raw MAP power
contents.support: Supports the commuting-covariance weighted minimizer and exact Gaussian size/power calculation; the local proof states the polar partial-isometry domain explicitly.

contents.name: Unrestricted null level-one obstruction for a non-eigenfeature
contents.locator: Theorem 2.6 and complete proof, PDF pp. 14–16
contents.support: Supports the null-direction scaling obstruction under the source's commutation and non-eigenfeature hypotheses; the local proof gives the direction and tail limit.

contents.name: Same-sample posterior/prior tuning does not inherit the fixed-prior power formula
contents.support: Supports the explicit caveat that the fixed-prior theorem does not certify same-sample empirical covariance tuning.

contents.name: Finite-dimensional non-eigenfeature calculation
contents.support: Provides context for the worked two-dimensional non-eigenfeature example; all coordinates and tail probabilities are recalculated locally.

sources.title: Remo Kretschmann, Tanja Wachsmuth, and Frank Werner, Optimal regularized hypothesis testing in statistical inverse problems
sources.locator: §1.1–1.3, Assumption 1, and Theorem 2.3 with its proof (PDF pp. 1–10); §3.2 same-data caveat.
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 32-page PDF and read the full indexed-noise model, the adjoint-range condition for unregularized probes, Assumption 1, Theorem 2.3 and its proof, and the same-data tuning qualification. The local calibrated-test proof derives the Gaussian tail bound directly for the specified Hilbert truth ball.

contents.name: Exact feature probes require an adjoint-range representation
contents.support: Provides an independent inverse-problem treatment of the exact range restriction for a single linear probe.

contents.name: Regularized probe test with deterministic approximation-error calibration
contents.locator: Assumption 1 and Theorem 2.3 proof, PDF pp. 5–10
contents.support: Supports the calibration by noise quantile plus the dual norm of the probe-feature discrepancy; the local proof verifies the level bound from the null and source-ball hypotheses.

sources.title: Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 705-page book PDF and read the full white-noise functional/sequence-model passages and the cited Gaussian example. The book gives the independent-standard-normal coordinate convention and emphasizes that the coefficient observation lives in a sequence space rather than generally in l2. It is used as the independent book treatment of the white-noise model, not as a proof of the MAP test theorem.

contents.name: Functional white noise and independent orthonormal coordinates
contents.support: Supports the coordinate and non-H-valued observation convention used to reconstruct the field sigma-algebra locally.

contents.name: Gaussian observation coordinate model context
contents.support: Provides independent Gaussian sequence-model context; the finite-dimensional exact estimator is derived locally.

contents.name: Diagonal Gaussian sequence model context
contents.support: Provides Gaussian sequence-model context; compactness, dense range, and failure of exact range membership are proved locally.

sources.title: Andrew M. Stuart, Inverse problems: A Bayesian perspective
sources.locator: §6.3, Theorem 6.20 and Example 6.23, formulas (6.14)–(6.16); §2.3 posterior and Tikhonov discussion (PDF pp. 58–66 and 13–17).
sources.reading_verification: Inspected the complete 110-page PDF and read the Gaussian conditioning theorem, its worked covariance formulas, and the posterior/Tikhonov discussion. This is an independent full-text treatment of Gaussian inverse-problem conditioning; the local proof supplies the infinite-cylinder RCD construction and feature-specific exceptional-set qualification.

contents.name: Gaussian conditioning and posterior mean/covariance operators
contents.support: Provides the independent Gaussian conditioning formulas for the posterior covariance and mean.

contents.name: Gaussian feature posterior and Tikhonov interpretation
contents.support: Supports the linear Gaussian posterior feature mean used by the scalar MAP comparison. The local raw rule is defined for every field input; its posterior-mode interpretation holds only P_Y-almost surely for each fixed feature, matching the actual posterior-law supplier.
